description:
Research a public repository or package to answer a question with sources. Omit target and thread_id for project identification. If Research returns candidates, retry with the one matching established context as target; never guess. Use pkg_info for registry metadata or repository URLs, package tools for assessments, and read for known symbols. Reuse thread_id for follow-ups; state scope changes. Ask for missing information; sources are included. Use and cite a sufficient answer directly. Open sources only for a specific missing detail, contradiction, or explicit source-inspection request; citations are not a reading checklist. Request an overview only when needed. A rate limit covers all Research questions/targets: wait the returned delay, or use direct retrieval for a specific gap; daily limits wait until reset.

Load the GitHits guide once per session first (`quick_start` or the `githits-mcp` skill).

format.description: Omit for text. Use json only when code consumes raw fields or text lacks a required field.

question.description: Focused research question about missing information for the task. Sources are included. Do not include credentials, personal data, private code, or proprietary content.

source_format.description: Source pointer format. `mcp` returns read calls for opening a source only when needed; `url` returns original upstream HTTP URLs.

target.description: Optional canonical open-source package or repository target, such as npm:express or github:expressjs/express. Never a docs site (site:): research covers the project's code and docs. Omit target and thread_id to identify the target from the question.

thread_id.description: Omit when no thread was returned; never pass an empty string. Otherwise reuse the returned thread UUID for follow-ups, without target; name scope changes in the question.

name: research
